To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the salience of visual speech information can exert a strong influence over both early and late stages in spoken-word recognition.
visual speech information can influence the processing of auditory speech at both early and late stages in sentence context.
the saliety of visual speech information exerts an influence over both early and late stages during spoken word recognition.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how audio-visual speech is processed in the brain, and how this processing relates to higher levels of speech comprehension.

the interactivity between audio and visual speech information during natural speech comprehension, and the constraints that visual information exerts on early and later stages of spoken-word processing in the brain.
understanding the role that audio-visual integration might play in spoken language comprehension.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

visual speech information is used to facilitate the recognition of words in natural speech context, but the effect of visual information is not restricted to the early stages of processing, and it may be modulated by the semantic predictability of words.
visual constraints are exerted at early and late stages, but the precise nature of this effect depends on the task and the level of analysis.
the visual information is used to constrain the auditory input at the early stages of processing and also at the later ones, but it is not used in the same manner at both levels.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

visual speech information can constrain both auditory processing and spoken-word recognition, and this effect is modulated by the degree of predictability of a word from a semantic sentential context.
visual information constrains early stages of spoken-word processing, and also late stages of spoken word processing in sentence context.
visual information constrains early stages of auditory word processing and late stages of semantic processing.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the saliencies of both the visual and auditory information are integrated at the early and late stages in speech comprehension.

the saliencies of the visual and auditory speech channels interact with each other, in a way that is not only dependent on the relative timing of the two signals but also on the relative strengths of their contributions to the overall speech signal.
the integration of visual speech information is not limited to the initial stages of speech processing but can also exert an influence on the recognition of spoken words at a later time.
